analysis.market_summary: Nifty slipped further (-0.62% to 23750, -1.37% over 5 days) as an IT-led selloff deepened on Fed rate-hike fears, while crude near $97/barrel stoked inflation worries. RBI held the repo rate steady and projected 6.9% GDP growth, but PSU/power names (Coal India, Power Grid) and select autos/pharma held up or gained even as Infosys, Tech Mahindra and HCLTech dropped 2-4%.
analysis.market_summary_plain: Indian stocks fell again mostly because tech/IT companies got hit hard on fears the US will keep interest rates high, and rising oil prices are making people worry about inflation; but power and coal companies actually went up because India is short on coal for power plants.

picks.name: Coal India
picks.thesis: Coal India is up 5.39% over 5 days and gained again yesterday as headlines describe power plants at critical coal levels and India ramping up rail shipments of coal - a direct tailwind for the country's dominant coal producer's volumes and pricing.
picks.plain_english: This company digs up coal, and India's power plants are running low on it, so more coal needs to be bought and shipped right now.
picks.catalysts: Continued reports of critical power-plant coal stocks; further rail shipment ramp-ups; any coal price/linkage hikes
picks.risks: If the crisis narrative cools quickly or monsoon/import coal eases shortages, the tailwind fades

picks.name: Power Grid Corporation of India
picks.thesis: Power Grid was named the top Nifty gainer yesterday and is up 1.57% over 5 days, holding firm while the broader index and IT stocks sold off, as the coal/power-supply crunch headlines put grid infrastructure back in focus.
picks.plain_english: This company owns the power lines that carry electricity across India, and it is one of the few stocks going up while most others fall.
picks.catalysts: More power-crisis headlines increasing focus on grid capacity; PSU/infra rotation as investors avoid IT
picks.risks: Rate-sensitive utility valuations could compress further if bond yields keep rising

picks.name: ICICI Bank
picks.thesis: Goldman Sachs just raised its price target on ICICI Bank citing deposit strength, and LIC received RBI approval to buy up to a 9.99% stake - a strong vote of confidence that helped the stock rise 0.25% even as the broader market fell. This is a repeat pick from yesterday, where it was the only one of five recent calls to beat the index (+0.22% alpha), supporting continued conviction.
picks.plain_english: India's biggest insurance company just got approved to buy a big stake in this bank, and a major Wall Street bank just said the stock deserves a higher price.
picks.catalysts: LIC stake purchase progressing; further broker upgrades on credit growth improving across private banks
picks.risks: Broader banking sector (BANKBEES) is still down on the day, so a market-wide risk-off move could still drag it lower

picks.name: Apollo Hospitals
picks.thesis: Apollo Hospitals rose 1.02% yesterday, one of the day's top gainers, and appeared in a 'festive stock picks' list - showing the stock catching bids even as the broader tape and IT names sold off hard.
picks.plain_english: This hospital chain's stock went up while most of the market went down, and analysts are recommending it as a buy ahead of the festival shopping season.
picks.catalysts: Inclusion in more festive/analyst buy lists; healthcare demand staying resilient to macro noise
picks.risks: Stock is still down 1.80% over 5 days, so the bounce could be short-lived if the broader selloff resumes

picks.name: Eicher Motors
picks.thesis: Eicher Motors gained 0.80% on record Q1 sales and a targeted capacity expansion to 2.45M units by FY30 - concrete fundamental progress that let the stock buck the market's downward drift.
picks.plain_english: This motorcycle maker (Royal Enfield) just reported its best-ever quarterly sales and plans to build a lot more bikes by 2030.
picks.catalysts: Continued strong monthly sales prints; capacity expansion updates
picks.risks: Stock is still down 3.29% over 5 days, and two-wheeler demand is sensitive to fuel-cost-driven consumer sentiment

picks.name: Maruti Suzuki
picks.thesis: Maruti announced a price hike of up to ₹20,000 on select models from September, a sign of pricing power and confident demand, and the stock rose 0.74% on the news even after a rough 5.60% slide over the prior week - suggesting the selloff may be overdone.
picks.plain_english: India's biggest car maker is raising prices because demand is strong enough to support it, and the stock bounced on that news after falling hard the past week.
picks.catalysts: Festive-season car demand pickup; further price hikes signaling margin support
picks.risks: Price hikes could dent volumes if demand is weaker than assumed; broader auto sector remains rate-sensitive

picks.name: Bharat Electronics
picks.thesis: BEL reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 25% to ₹5,533 crore on strong execution, and the stock still edged up 0.23% despite a broad market selloff driven by oil and rate fears - a sign the defense PSU's earnings strength is being recognized.
picks.plain_english: This defense electronics maker just reported revenue growing a quarter faster than last year, and its stock held up even while the market fell.
picks.catalysts: Continued strong order execution; defense sector PSU re-rating
picks.risks: Stock still down 1.97% over 5 days; a prior pick on this name (conviction 4) was roughly flat, so momentum has been modest

picks.name: Asian Paints
picks.thesis: Despite falling 1.27% yesterday and 5.97% over 5 days on crude-driven input-cost worries, headlines report paint makers seeing 'strong festive growth' and Asian Paints/Berger holding demand despite rising costs - a potential buy-the-dip setup once oil-driven input-cost fears ease.
picks.plain_english: This paint company is selling more paint for the festival season even though the raw materials it needs (oil-based) are getting pricier, and the stock has already fallen a lot.
picks.catalysts: Festive demand data confirming strength; crude prices stabilizing
picks.risks: If crude keeps rising toward/above $97, margin compression fears could keep pressuring the stock further

picks.name: Tata Consumer Products
picks.thesis: Tata Consumer approved a ₹10 dividend at its AGM and was named among top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying this volatile week, giving it a defensive, income-generating profile as the broader market wobbles; however this same name was picked yesterday and posted a slightly negative alpha (-0.30%), so conviction is tempered.
picks.plain_english: This tea, coffee and packaged-food company just approved a cash payout to shareholders and analysts are calling it a buy during this shaky market week.
picks.catalysts: Dividend record-date buying interest; defensive rotation out of IT and into FMCG
picks.risks: Prior day's pick of this name underperformed the index slightly, showing momentum has been weak so far

picks.name: Larsen & Toubro
picks.thesis: L&T edged up 0.19% even as the broader market fell on oil/Fed worries, and its subsidiary L&T Technology Services confirmed no promoter share encumbrance - a stability signal; this is a repeat pick from yesterday which slightly underperformed (-0.28% alpha), so conviction is kept low.
picks.plain_english: This large construction and engineering company's stock rose slightly even as the wider market fell, and its promoters confirmed they haven't pledged their shares as loan collateral, which is reassuring.
picks.catalysts: Continued domestic capex/infra order wins; PSU/infra rotation away from IT
picks.risks: Yesterday's identical pick already underperformed the index, so this signal has not yet proven itself

etf_picks.name: Nippon CPSE ETF
etf_picks.thesis: With Coal India and Power Grid both showing relative strength amid the coal/power supply crunch headlines, and CPSEETF itself up 1.26% over 5 days while the Nifty fell, this basket of government-owned companies is capturing exactly the PSU/power theme driving today's gainers.
etf_picks.plain_english: This fund holds a basket of India's big government-owned companies, including the coal and power firms that are going up while the rest of the market struggles with a power shortage.
etf_picks.risks: PSU stocks can be volatile around policy news and are sensitive to any resolution of the coal shortage narrative

etf_picks.name: Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100
etf_picks.thesis: MON100 jumped 3.67% in a single day, sharply diverging from the beaten-down Indian IT sector (ITBEES -2.35%) - suggesting US big tech strength is intact even as Fed rate fears are hammering Indian IT services stocks, making this a way to get tech exposure away from the domestic IT selloff.
etf_picks.plain_english: This fund lets Indian investors own big US tech giants like Apple and Microsoft, and it jumped a lot even while Indian tech stocks were falling.
etf_picks.risks: It is priced in rupee terms and exposed to US rate decisions and dollar/rupee moves; a real Fed hike could still hurt US tech too

etf_picks.name: Nippon Nifty Pharma BeES
etf_picks.thesis: Pharma was the only sector ETF to close flat-to-positive (+0.07%) yesterday while IT and the broader index fell, consistent with defensive positioning during a rate-fear and oil-driven selloff, and 'Top pharma stocks to buy' headlines suggest ongoing sector interest.
etf_picks.plain_english: This fund holds a basket of Indian drug and healthcare companies, which held steady while almost everything else in the market fell.
etf_picks.risks: Company-specific pharma risks exist (e.g., FDA inspection issues at Dr. Reddy's) that could weigh on individual holdings within the fund

watchlist.name: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories
watchlist.reason: US FDA issued a Form 483 after inspecting its Srikakulam unit - watch for resolution or further regulatory news before buying

watchlist.name: Tata Consultancy Services
watchlist.reason: Hit a 52-week low despite announcing a new AI-native studio and a ₹70,000 crore Hyderabad AI data centre investment - watch for stabilization before entering the broader IT-sector selloff

watchlist.name: Trent
watchlist.reason: Fell 2.33% despite a brokerage seeing 27% upside on the retail stock - conflicting signals, worth watching for a clearer direction

avoid.name: Infosys
avoid.reason: Led IT-sector losses, down 3.60% in a day and 3.92% over 5 days, purely on macro Fed rate-hike fears with no offsetting company-specific positive catalyst in the headlines

avoid.name: Wipro
avoid.reason: Goldman Sachs maintained a 'Sell' rating with a target below the current price (~3% downside), and the stock is already down 6.17% over 5 days

avoid.name: Jio Financial Services
avoid.reason: MarketsMojo rates it a 'Sell' and the stock fell 1.76% despite a 156% YoY profit jump, suggesting the market isn't rewarding the earnings beat
